comments.value: It's only natural with the rise of eye tracking! We need this!

This would be fantastic, though I totally diasgree with using winking as a method to click for a bunch of reasons.

VRC's menu design would need a major overhaul to handle this though, as the current trend of turning everything into endless lists of lists is not good for this kind of input.

Or any kind of input to be honest.

@{5f2d38467f57433511425209|full_name}: "wink" was there mostly as I want the ability to trigger clicks from the outside for flexibility and more options. I agree that it's not the best example, realistically it might be a standalone clicker or some other method like EEG concentration levels, timed long stare, etc.

VRC could change their menu, but if you allowed controller triggers, navigating wouldn't really be any more of an issue than with a controller normally. 

Would I like to see it in the future? Sure. But it's by no means a requirement.
turning vrchat into a full operating system. VRChatOS?

details:
We have native eye tracking support now and that's great!

Though I feel like it should be used to it's full potential more via menu interactions.

The idea:

Use eye gaze data to act like another pointer for menus and world interaction.

There could be a setting to allow for a trigger on your (left or right) controller to trigger ET gaze pointer click.

Ideally there would also be an OSC address to toggle this externally. (say the external eye tracking software like EyeTrackVR can send a click when the user winks)

For example with the setting on, looking at the "worlds" button and an app sending a True value to the OSC address: "/tracking/eye/PointerClick" would cause a trigger press on that button.

Thanks for your time.
title: Eye Tracking Menu Interactions
